notes: RULE 3 / AUTHENTICITY: genuine corporate storefront of Cello World Limited (BSE/NSE-listed Indian houseware manufacturer). /pages/contact-us gives the real corporate office - 'Cello World Limited, Cello House, Corporate Avenue, Sonawala Industry Estate, Goregaon (E), Mumbai 400063' - and site meta keywords name 'Cello World Limited'. Not a reseller/impersonation site (S.N. 109 Alinea precedent checked). Catalogue is LIVE, not retired or redirected. ACCESS ROUTE: plain direct curl with a desktop UA, first try, no WAF, no bypass needed. www.celloworld.com 301s to https://celloworld.com. robots.txt has ONE generic 'User-Agent: *' group (Allow: / plus Disallow of /api/*, /account/*, /cart/*, /*.json$, /*/order/*) - NO ClaudeBot/Claude-User/Claude-SearchBot/Claude-Web disallow, so the Amazon/Home24 precedent does not apply. The Disallow of /*.json$ and /api/* was respected: no products.json and no internal API endpoint was called; every number below comes from the ordinary HTML of the category page itself. LANGUAGE: site renders 100% in English natively (INR pricing, en lang attribute); no Hindi or regional-language category names anywhere, so no translation was needed. PLATFORM & COUNT METHOD (RULE 1): headless Shopify behind a Next.js/Vercel front end (product IDs are gid://shopify/Product/..., images on cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0801/3922/3334). The category pages render NO 'N products' header at all, so there is no site-reported count string to quote. Instead every category page server-renders its complete product list into the React Server Component flight payload as 'initialProducts' with a Shopify pageInfo. Every category checked came back with pageInfo.hasNextPage=false, i.e. the payload is the whole collection, so each qty is an exhaustive enumeration of DISTINCT gid://shopify/Product IDs - not an API total. VARIANT-INFLATION TRAP CONFIRMED AND AVOIDED: the same payload carries 'initialFilters.price.count', which looks like a product total but is a VARIANT total. Proof: /collections/all-products enumerates 179 distinct products while price.count says 577; /collections/tableware enumerates 27 products vs count 48; /collections/glassware 9 vs 15; /collections/kidzbee-dinner-set 7 vs 35. Had that field been trusted, every qty would have been 2-5x too high (same class of error as the Design Public Algolia nbHits case). All qty values below are the deduplicated distinct-product counts. CATALOGUE SIZE CROSS-CHECK: the whole D2C site is only 179 live products (/collections/all-products, hasNextPage=false). The site's own sitemap.xml lists 223 /products/ URLs, but the 44 extras are stale - spot-checked https://celloworld.com/products/solitaire-opalware-dinner-set-ruby-nw, which renders the 404 page. So 179 is the real live catalogue and the leaf counts below are consistent with it. SCOPE / STRUCTURE: the mega menu has 11 top-level nodes - Hydration, Personalize, Tableware, Kitchen, Tiffin Boxes, Cookware, Appliances, Cleaning Essential, Kidzbee, Porcelain, Glassware (plus a Gifting node whose collections are all EMPTY, and which would be excluded as a gift guide regardless). Only four branches are in scope and all four are filed under Kitchen & Dining: Tableware (opalware dinner sets, bowl/tea/snack sets, cup & saucer), Porcelain (mugs), Glassware (drinking glass, beer mugs) and the Tableware sub-branch of Kidzbee. EXCLUDED, with the reason: Hydration (51 products - water bottles, flasks, travel tumblers = hydration/thermoware, not tableware); Tiffin Boxes and all lunch-box/bento nodes (food storage); Kitchen > Casseroles (both the insulated hot-pot casseroles and the Angelica glass casserole - casserole-as-cookware/thermoware, not serveware) and Kitchen > Jar and Containers (food storage); Cookware (tawa, kadhai, pressure cooker, cast iron, non-stick sets); Appliances (mixer grinders, air fryers, induction cooktops, juicers, sandwich makers); Cleaning Essential (dustbins, mops, spin scrubber); Personalize (a customisation programme over flasks); and the non-tableware Kidzbee nodes (bottles, flasks, lunch boxes, bathroom set, backpacks, cupboards/storage). No plastic moulded furniture or writing-instrument division appears on this site at all. JUDGMENT CALL DOCUMENTED PER BRIEF - opalware/melamine: dinner sets, snack/dessert/tea sets, cups, saucers, plates, bowls and mugs are IN (they are dinnerware/serveware); food-storage containers, lunch boxes and insulated casseroles carrying similar 'set' names are OUT. Product titles were read individually on every mixed node rather than trusting node names - e.g. Kidzbee 'Bowls' turned out to be 'Cone Kids Melamine Bowl, Set of 3' (dinnerware, IN) while Kidzbee 'Storage' is plastic cupboards (OUT). Kids melamine/opalware meal sets and plates are included as dinnerware; the two Kids Mugs items are 'No Drop Kids Anti-Fall Tumbler 350 ml' and 'No Drop Kids Anti-Fall Mug 400 ml', i.e. drinkware rather than bottles, so they are IN. MATERIAL/FACET RE-CUTS DROPPED (product-ID sets compared, not names): /collections/opalware holds exactly the same 16 product IDs as /collections/dinner-sets, and /collections/dinnerware (23) is a roll-up of dinner-sets 16 + the kids dinner sets; neither is in the navigation, so both were dropped rather than emitted as extra rows. /collections/gifting and its seven children, plus /collections/porcelain-cups-and-saucer, porcelain-deep-bowl, porcelain-platters, mugs, tumblers-1 and serveware-glass-mixing-bowl, are all EMPTY collections (0 products) and were dropped. PARENT-VS-CHILD ARITHMETIC: Tableware parent enumerates 27 = 16+2+2+4+3, an exact match. Porcelain parent enumerates 6, identical to its only child Porcelain Mugs. Glassware parent enumerates 9 vs 5+3=8 children; the orphan is 'Ornella Glass Mixing Bowl', a kitchen-prep mixing bowl that sits in no navigation leaf and would be out of scope anyway. Kids Tableware parent enumerates 13 vs 7+3+2+1=13, but there is a real overlap - 'Cone Kids Melamine Bowl, Set of 3' appears in BOTH kidzbee-dinner-set and kidzbee-bowls - and one parent-only item ('Kids Opal Snack Set, 5 Piece') sits in no leaf; each leaf qty is still that leaf's own exact enumerated count. RULE 0 / LIGHTING & MIRRORS - ABSENCE CONFIRMED, NOT ASSUMED: there is no lighting, mirror, clock, vase, wall-art, candle-holder or planter category anywhere in the navigation, and the check was done against the site's own data rather than by assumption - the complete 179-product catalogue at /collections/all-products was enumerated and every product title and productType inspected. The productType vocabulary is entirely houseware (Dinner Sets, Tea Set, Snack Set, Cup and Saucer, Bowl Set, Mugs, Tumbler, Beer Mugs, Glass Mixing Bowl, Bottles, Flask, Insulated, Plastics, Cookware types, Mixer Grinder, Air Fryer, Dustbin, Backpacks, Storage...). Zero lighting, zero mirrors, zero clocks. Note the site search page is client-rendered and its server HTML returns a default product set regardless of the query, so it is useless as an absence test; the full-catalogue enumeration is the stronger evidence and was used instead. NO DUPLICATE-COMPANY FLAG applies to S.N. 260; celloworld.com has not been extracted before in this project. First India-market company in the project.
